description: Lady Alice was a chance seeding discovered in 1979. This apple is supposed to have a long shelf life, and taste better as it ages, at its best in March, but i don't think so. It's very crisp with a unique tangy flavour, almost like candy. 8/10

Gala is a cross between Kidds Orange Redd, and a Golden Delicious. A little sweet, a little tart, pretty watery. This apple is currently the most popular apple in north america, and is the parent of many other apples.

The royal gala apple is a sport of a gala apple, meaning that due to a mutation, it's exactly the same as a regular gala, but more red. There are currently 24 known named gala sports
5/10

Despite the name, it's not a different coloured Gala apple, instead it's a cross between a Gala and a Splendour. This is a very sweet apple, and may have a pinkish-red blush. The apples with bigger blushes and more dots (lenticels) are incredibly sweet. It's one of my favourite apples, and its the apple that got me interested in apples in the first place. 9/10
Jazz is a cross between the Gala and Braeburn apples, and is a trademarked apple variety. Its official name is Scifresh. Its a very crunchy apple, with a slightly sour flavour. 6/10

Envy doesn't look or taste similar to a Jazz apple, but it is also a cross between a Gala and Braeburn. Envy is also a trademarked name, its official name is Scilate, and it was created by the same people who made the Jazz apple. Its a crisp apple. Similar to the Orin apple, its quite dense, and fairly sweet. For some reason, this apple variety isn't very consistent. I've had many envy apples and some tasted great, some were just okay. Ill give it a 5/10.

Fuji is a cross between a Red Delicious and a Ralls Janet, created in Japan in the 1930s. It has a nice flavour, although its quite watered down.
Apparently these apples are a pain to grow; the trees don't fruit for the first few years, and then take another few years to bear fruit that tastes good.
5/10.
Pink Lady, also known as Cripps Pink, is a cross between Lady Williams and Golden Delicious. Its a softer apple, and a bit more sour than other apples. 7/10.

Spartan is a cross between a Mcintosh and an unknown apple, its supposed to be used in baking, not really for eating raw. Its a very soft apple, with thick, reddish-brown skin and bright white on the inside.
Although I do prefer crisp apples over softer varieties, I appreciate the flavour this apple offers. 5/10.

Opal is a cross between a golden delicious, and a topaz apple. It's yellow with dark lenticels, and appears to be russeted at the top. It's fairly sweet, and tastes a bit tart and floral, similar to an asian pear. The flesh is quite crisp. 7/10

Honeycrisp  is an interesting apple, it was bred specifically for taste, and so it has a terrible shelf life and bruises easily. It was originally created by the Minnesota Universitys apple breeding program, and thought to be a cross between Macoun and Honeygold. Later it was discovered to be a cross between Keepsake and MN1627 (which is a no longer existing apple variety also created by the Minnesota University). 

The apple tastes equally sweet and sour, and is incredibly crisp. Its crispness is attributed to the apple having larger cells, and therefore more cells rupture when bitten. Its a very good apple, for eating raw or baking. 

Unfortunately, the Honeycrisp apple will probably decline in quality over the years, like the red delicious. I think apple growers will prioritize growing honeycrisps with better shelf life, and easier shipping, which will lead to a worse tasting apple. I rate this iconic apple 8/10.

Cosmic Crisp is apple is pretty interesting, as it took over 20 years and $10million to develop and market the apple. 

The Honeycrisp apple is such a high demand apple, yet is so fragile, so I'm sure the Cosmic crisp aims to replace it.
The Cosmic crisp is a cross between a Honeycrisp and an Enterprise apple, and it has inherited most of the flavour and crispness of a Honeycrisp, while also having an extended shelf life and is more bruise resistant. 

For the taste, it's very similar to a Honeycrisp , and I would say its even more crisp. However, it's thicker skin is noticeable, and slightly bitter. 7/10

Granny Smith is fairly tart, like an orange, and has thicker skin. It's mostly used as a cooking apple since it holds its shape well, and isn't very sweet. For some reason, it's my dad's favourite apple.
I prefer sweet apples over sour apples, so I give this a 4/10.

Ambrosia is a chance seeding thats thought to be a cross between a golden delicious and a red delicious. It's fairly crisp and quite sweet, but with very little flavour.
5/10

Red Delicious is a very old variety; originally named 'Hawkeye' it was sold to Stark nurseries, who renamed it to 'Stark Delicious'. After the Golden Delicious apple became fairly popular, the Stark delicious apple was renamed'Red Delicious'.

This apple used to live up to its name, but over time, it was bred to look nice and ship well at the cost of tasting worse. It has thick, bitter skin, and although its fairly sweet, it tastes bland. The flesh is a little crisp, but also has a texture similar to mud. 

2/10

Rockit is apple was pretty good, it's very sweet, and incredibly crisp, and has a faint bitterish taste similar to a red delicious, but without the awful grainy texture. This apple is tiny; barely larger than a golf ball. Because of it's small size, it's heavily marketed as the 'worlds first snack size apple', which is silly.There are many other apples that are small like this one. 6/10.

Sugarbee tastes pretty similar to an ambrosia apple, very sweet but with little flavour. However, it's more crisp than ambrosia.
6/10.

Despite being a green-yellow colour, Orin is not sour at all. Its quite sweet like a golden gala, and while the skin is crisp and thin, the flesh is more soft. What makes this apple interesting is its flavour, it tastes more like a pear than an apple, and it has dense flesh, also like a pear. I thought this apple was very good, much better than a lot of other apples I've tried. If you are a fan of sweet apples, I highly suggest you try this one.

I bought this apple at a farmers market in Calgary, and one of the workers told me it was a cross between an apple and a pear. You cant crossbreed apples and pears, so i'm not sure why she said that. The Orin apple is actually a cross between a Golden delicious and an Indo apple. 
I rate this apple 9/10, and it's currently my favourite apple.

Kanzi is a very nice variety. It's a cross between a gala and a braeburn, like the jazz and envy apples. It seems to be more similar to the jazz apple though, its definitely crisp, and has a light, honeycrisp-like flavour. Its fairly sour, but a little less sour than a granny smith. Because of the kanzis large size, it seems to be a bit watery, but thats not too noticeable. 8/10, a great apple for those who prefer them sour.

Koru is okay. Its a cross between a Braeburn and Fuji, and the first tree grew from an apple core tossed i to a rose garden. It's similar to an ambrosia or gala, in that it tastes quite sweet and lacking in flavour. 

I was mildly disappointed by the flavour, as the Koru apple is marketed as a "spicy but sweet" apple, and it is unfortunately not spicy in the slightest. Another of the Koru apples slogans is "Escape Ordinary' which is bizarre because this apple is nothing special. It's not bad, just doesn't live up to the expectations it sets. On the plus side, this apple takes a while to brown when sliced. If you find one of these apples in the store, I don't suggest buying any. 4/10.

Jonagold was brought to me by my sibling, who bought it in Halifax.

The Jonagold apple gets its name from its parents, the Golden delicious, and Jonathan apples. It tastes pretty similar to a gala apple; Faintly sweet, and with a dry flavour. Im glad to have gotten to try this apple, although it's not one I would likely try again. 5/10

Smitten is probably one of the more interesting looking ones I've seen so far, The stem is incredibly thick, and the bottom of the apple around the calyx has pronounced ridges, similar but not as large as a Red Delicious. The skin also has a a very nice pattern and colour.

When I was researching this apple, I was quite surprised to find out it had 4 parents. I had heard of apples have 2 or 3 parents, but never 4. Some varieties of apple trees are triploids, which means they have more than 2 parents, and therefore have more than 2 sets of chromosomes and may have difficulty with pollination.

The Smitten apple is a cross between a Gala, Braeburn, Fiesta, and Falstaff. Lots of good apples have Gala and Braeburn as parents.

 As for the Smitten apple itself, its quite crisp, and it tastes like to a watered down honeycrisp, with a bit of gala apple. Overall, this is apple is interesting because of its unique 4 parents, but honestly it doesn't taste good enough to buy again. 6/10

I have no idea what kind of apple this is. 
I found the tree in the Place de la Gare park in Quebec city. The tree produced hundreds, maybe thousands of apples, which littered the ground around it.

This tiny apple, which i assume is a type of crab-apple or apple-crab, is quite tart and had mildly bitter skin, like a granny smith. Not soft, it was actually very crisp, and tasted a bit dry. Overall I'll give it a 4/10.

This is the second apple tree I found in the Place de la Gare. I also have no clue what this apple is called. 

This apple tree had the same sized apples, although much less of them on than the first tree. These apples were bright red, so from a distance it could be mistaken for a cherry tree.

These apples were pretty similar to the ones i got from the other tree, although slightly juicier and more sour. These apples also seemed to have thinner skin, and tasted less like a Granny smith, and more comparable to a very sour Fuji. I give this apple a 4/10 as well.
Crabapple from hazeldell orchard in Kelowna. The name of it is unknown, and it's quite tart. Unfortunately, this apple browns quite quickly,after 5 mins it was very brown. 6/10

Like many apples that start with the letter S, the Silken variety was developed in Summerland B.C. It's quite an ugly apple, pale skin, slightly knobby, and with russetting at the top. Although it looks sour, this apple was more on the sweet side. It tastes like a Granny Smith thats just barely sour, with notes of honey. If you enjoy Granny Smith, I recommend you give this apple a try. 7/10

Nova Spy is very sour, but also fairly sweet and crisp. It similar to a honeycrisp 
6/10, too sour for me

Lucy Glo is probably the coolest variety I've tried so far.
Its a cross between a Honeycrisp and a Hidden rose apple, the latter of which is responsible for its red flesh. The Hidden Rose apple is a descendant of the Niedzwetzkyana apple, an awful tasting apple with blood red flesh.

As for the taste, Lucy Glo is really good, its quite sweet and tart, and interestingly tastes kind of like wild berries. Highly recommend it, I might be a bit biased because of the cool colour of its flesh, but i give it 10/10.

This apple was brought to me by Declan Armstrong

Not to be confused with Lucy glo, Lucy Rose is a cross between a Honeycrisp and a Hidden Rose, the latter of which gives it its mottled red flesh. Like all red fleshed apples, its a descendent of the niedzwetzkyana apple. After tasting how good the Lucy Glo apple was, I was excited to try the Lucy Rose, which unfortunately isn't great. It just tastes like a Gala, maybe slightly more sour. However, I will say its very crisp, like the honeycrisp. If you have the chance to try either of the lucy apples, I suggest skipping this one in favour of the Glo. 5/10.

I bought Pazzazz in a grocery store in America and couldn't take it across the border to get a nice picture of it.

This apple is a cross between a honeycrisp and an unknown apple. It's like a softer honeycrisp, with slightly thicker skin. It's not bad, but nothing special 6/10.

Lodi apple, from Wlonka farms in Creston BC
This is a cross between a Yellow Transparent and a Montgomery Sweet. Like Transparent, it's a very early season apple, and is quite tart. It's about as sour as granny smith, but it's less sweet, thinner skin, and more mealy, like a red delicious. It's better suited for making applesauce than for eating raw. As I do rate these apples out of how good they are raw, the Lodi apple gets a 2/10.

Sunrise is a cross between Golden Delicious and Macintosh, this apple is pretty good. It's super dense and crunchy, tastes sweet and just a little sour. The skin isn't super thick, but it is noticeable. This apple gets an 8/10, I would buy it again.

Transparent was bad. It was dry, had little flavour and was so soft I couldn't split it in half; the skin would just smush off. It was kind of sour, not very sweet. The flesh of this apple was so soft, it was like eating a red delicious that had been bruised all over, or maybe like really fine grained mud. 

This apple is best used for pie, not fresh eating. Most places say the Transparent apple is very sour, and very flavourful. That was not my experience but maybe I got an apple at the edge of its very short shelf life (~10 days). I may have to revisit this apple variety.

'Transparent apples' can refer to the White Transparent, or Yellow Transparent. However, these varieties are so similar that some people do not care to differentiate them.

I feel a little bad judging this apple so harshly on the fresh eating aspect, since it's not grown for this. With that said, I did not enjoy eating this apple. It is the first apple I will grant the rating of 1/10.

This is a crabapple from Eli Ambrosio's tree. It was mildly dry and bitter, but overall not too sour for a crabapple. 

The red flesh means it's most likely not a random tree, and is instead a known variety of apple. A red-fleshed apple generally has red-pink flowers, which makes me think this is an ornamental crabapple variety bred specifically for those coloured leaves. 

As for the rating, it's a crabapple. Not great. But I've had worse apples, 3/10

Earligold was very soft, but quite sour and just sweet enough, with a very pleasant , light flavour that I can't quite discern. (A faint taste of concord grape?) It's not too soft like Transparent, but the softness really compliments its flavour. This is probably my favourite soft apple, I would buy it again.

This apple is slow to brown, and keeps well. It ripens early in the season, hence the name. It's parents are unknown.

This apple changed my mind about soft apples, they can be good too and aren't all grainy and mushy like red delicious. I rate this: 8/10

Wynoochee Early is a smaller apple, and I found it to be tart but still sweet, and very dense. It tastes similar to a Granny Smith, but without the overbearing bitter flavour from the skin. Not a bad apple, 6/10

Previously believed to be four different crabapples, but seeing as they were almost indistinguishable and found in the same area, I'll count them as one variety. I tried them on a walk to the bar. None of them were good. All were varying degrees of sour and bitter. 2/10

Like a Jonagold apple, Jonaprince is a cross between the Jonathan and Golden Delicious varieties. It tastes pretty similar to Jonagold. Its sour more than sweet, crisp but not super dense, the taste of its skin is a little more noticeable than other varieties. Nothing special about this apple, I rate it 5/10.

Ginger gold is a chance seedling from a golden delicious apple, and possibly Albermarle Pippin. Unlike most early season apples, Ginger Gold is very slow to oxidize and has a long shelf life. Preserve shape well when cooked. Not named ginger because like the spice, it's actually named after the guy who first cultivated it, his nickname was "Ginger".

On the softer side, sweet and barely tart. Skin is really thin, not noticeable at all. I would describe the texture as smooth. Kind of juicy, but also kind of dry. Mild flavour. 7/10

McIntosh is the national apple of canada. Kind of sour, fairly sweet, it's much better than I remember. Though the skin is thicker than other apples, it doesn't have a distinct bitter taste to it. I rate it 8/10, this apple is so good it makes me a little patriotic.

Golden Delicious is one of the better golden deliciouses I've had. Pretty sweet, barely sour, no mealy texture like red delicious. The skin is thin, not noticeable. It's a cross between Grimes Golden and an unknown apple. Despite the name, it's not closely related to Red Delicious. Apparently it's good for baking die to it's high pectin content. Some popular apples that are children of this apple are Gala, Honeycrisp, Ambrosia, Lady Williams, Jonagold, and one of my favourites, Opal.
I rate this apple 7/10

Hidden rose is more tart than sweet, with hints of strawberry lemonade. Not as flavourful as Lucy Glo, but still pretty good. Amazing colour, the inside is a deep pink-red. It's parents are unknown, but like all red-fleshed apples, it's a descendant of Niedzwetzkyana. Hidden Rose is one of the parents of the Lucy Glo, and Lucy Rose varieties, both of which have pink flesh. 7/10

My university hosted an apple tasting event, there were a couple apples I hadn't tried before, like this one.

Salish is very crisp, equally tart and sweet. Pretty skin, uniform red with few yellow streaks, lightly dotted white. Like many apples, it's a cross between Gala and Splendour. Taste-wise, its quite similar to a honeycrisp. It's tastes good, though it's nothing special. 6/10

September Wonder is a sport of Fuji, so it doesn't taste much different.
Apple sports are varieties that come from a mutated branch. The September Wonder would've been growing on a regular fuji tree, but all the apples on the sport branch would've been slightly different from fujis. The new apples were so different (ripened earlier, russeted blotches, slightly more tart), that they were given a new name, September Wonder. 
Since September Wonders are a fuji sport, they don't taste all that different. I think it tastes almost identical to Fuji, though maybe a bit more tart.
7/10

PiÃ±ata is nicely tart and sweet, skin is thick, but not overwhelming. This apples flavour is more full than many others, its not bland at all. It's supposed to have an aftertaste of pineapple, but I didn't taste it. Interestingly, PiÃ±ata is a cross between 3 different varieties; Golden Delicious, Cox's Orange Pippin, and Duchess of Oldenburg. I would buy this apple over others like gala or fuji, I rate it 7/10

Crabapples in some liquid.
I thought the liquid would be vinegar, or some kind of brine, but opening up the jar it smelled like cinnamon. The apples inside were squishy, like rubber, but still firm and not mushy. It tasted like a heavily spiced apple pie, kind of nice. Definitely not my usual post, I don't know what kind of crabapple this is or what liquid they're submerged in. I rate itâ¦ 7/10? Its better than a gala, the spiced flavour is really nice but the texture is strange.

Nicola is another nice apple with the parents Gala and Splendour.
This apple is quite crisp, juicy, and has a stronger aromatic flavour than many other grocery store apples. It has a very long shelf life of around 5 months. Its deep red skin is pretty, and not bitter. Overall I rate this apple 8/10

I had been wanting to try Braeburn for a while, it's a parent of lots of good apples. Luckily managed to find this while on an extended flight layover. 
They're thought to be a cross between a Red Delicious and a Sturmer Pippen. They tast sweet, with a really nice sour aftertaste. Texture is a bit softer than other popular apples, but still nice. 7/10

Red Windsor is the first of many apples I get to try in Scotland. The Red Windsor apple is a sport of the Alkmene variety, meaning they're almost the same but the Red Windsor is more red, and  is supposed to have a sharper taste. 
Its a very dense, crisp apple. Its has a very strong sour taste, almost as sour as a granny smith, though its a bit more sweet. Overall I'd say this apple is very similar to a Granny Smith. I rate it 5/10, average.

Cox's Orange Pippin is a very pretty apple. Its mottled red and green, with streaks of brown russeting running from the stem. It's name comes from the farmer who grew it, Richard Cox (yes I'm serious that was his actual name). The word "pippin" used to be a word to describe a small fruit seed.
 Cox's Orange Pippin is a very old cultivar of apple, with 
79 known descendant apples, like Red Windsor, Fiesta, and 7 of the 27 'Laxton' varieties.
This apple is very flavourful. It's sweet and tart, more tart than a honeycrisp. Biting into it, the flesh is denser than most apples, but not overly so. Its skin is a bit thicker than most apples, but leaves a floral aftertaste. 
I rate it 9/10. It tasted nice, looked pretty, and I'd buy it again. No wonder it's the parent of so many tasty apples.

Bramley was first grown by Mary Ann Brailsford in 1809. The tree it grows on is resistant to apple scab and mildew. Its meant for baking, not for eating as a snack. It 
It tastes very sour, barely sweet. It's a very hard apple. I would like to make a pie or crumble or something with this, it seems even better than granny smith for cooking. Since this rating doesn't take its taste in baking into account, I have to give this a 3/10. So sour.

Russet apples such as Egremont Russet are apples that are pre-disposed to russeting more than usual apples. The russet texture is like fine sandpaper on the apples skin, and is caused by micro-cracks on its surface. Generally, russet apples like this one have a dry taste, more intense flavour, and are often used to make cider. The russeting on apples is the same as the russeting on Russet potatoes, or Bosc pears. Russeting can occur on regular apples too, just not super intensely. 

The Egremont russet is quite a dry, crunchy apple, like a firm pear. The skin feels dry and rough because of the russeting, but it doesn't leave a bitter aftertaste. This apple has a very unique flavour from any other apple I've tried. It tastes almost like a pear, though not as much as an Orin apple does. It has a faint underlying flavour of nuts, or cinnamon. It's nice and sweet but barely tart. 

This apple is awesome, I've been wanting to try a russet apple for a long time, and it has exceeded my expectations. I rate it 10/10, I definitely recommend you try it if you have the chance.
Pirouette tastes pretty good, nothing special, just a plain good apple. Its crisp, juicy, sweet and a bit tart. Reminds me of an ambrosia. It's apparently very popular with organic growers. 6/10

Zari is quite light, but still crisp and very juicy. It tastes very similar to Gala apples. Its a fairly new variety from belgium, introduced in 2008. Its parents are Elstar and Delbard Estivale. This apple is good, but nothing special. I rate it 5/10, just average.

Santana is much more sour than I was expecting. I haven't really had many sour red apples before. It tastes like a sour spartan or macintosh apple, though more crisp than either of those. What makes this apple special is it was developed with the goal of minimizing the amount of a specific protein that some people are allergic to. So if you know someone who is allergic to apples, get them to try Santana. I rate this apple 6/10

Rubens is quite sweet and barely sour. The texture is crisp and almost flakey, like an asian pear. 
This apple variety is also known as Civni, and it was developed by the Consorzio Italiano Vivaisti, an italian nursery who specializes in apples and strawberry plant research. I rate this apple 7/10

This unknown baking apple was definitely sour, but just sweet enough. It tasted kind of crab apple-y, though it was very juicy unlike most crabapples. 
I found this apple at the end of a 3 hour long hike, which may have made it taste a lot better than it should've. I rate it 7/10

Maribelle has a very mild flavour, the skin is fairly thick. The flavour is nice but there's just not very much of it. This apple variety is ripe from October to may, so maybe I just got some that were picked a little too early for the flavour to fully develop.
Maribelle is a triploid fruit, it has 3 parents: Gloster, Meiprinses, and Elstar. I rate it 4/10, its nice but the skin is quite thick

I picked Reinette up from a market in Italy. Rennet is a popular type of apple in Italy and Portugal. 
Reinette isn't a specific variety of apple, but instead an umbrella term for ~50 different cultivars. I'm not sure which variety of reinette this one is specifically, even after a deep dive on Wikipedia. 
I'm sure not all reinettes are bad, but this one is not very good. It's very soft, like a Transparent. It has a mild flavour which does nothing to distract from its thick skin and mud-like texture. This is not a good apple, I rate it 2/10

Samboa is the brand name for 3 different apple varieties, Luiza, Venice, and Isodora. Each of these apples were bred to be basically the same except harvested at different times of the year. Pretty cool, I've never heard of that before.
This apple is dry, like wine. It has a crisp bite, honeycrisp-like taste and texture, though sweeter. The sweetness is very prevalent, all other flavour is kind of hidden behind it. If it wasn't for the excessive sweetness it would be very nice, but the sugar in it is the main selling point for this apple.
I rate it 5/10

Not only is Scarlett Paradise very pretty, it also tastes great. Just the right amount of sour, it's also nicely sweet and juicy. It has a more prevalent flavour than other varieties, reminds me of Aurora Golden Gala, and other dessert apples. 
The only drawback is that it doesn't have a very long shelf life, lasting about 2 weeks. It's also only available at M&S foods in the UK. 
I've emailed the growers for more information about it, as there's not much available online, but they never responded.
I rate it 9/10, great apple.

Pixie is tiny! Just a little bigger than a mandarin orange. Because of its small size, it's not grown commercially. It seems to be a good apple for home growing though, as it's fairly disease resistant and requires low effort to maintain. Pixie trees tend to overcrop, and produce lots of little apples but you can get around this by pruning your trees each winter.
Pixie is a fairly normal tasting apple, with a bit of a sharp tang to it. The skins flavour is slightly noticeable, but it's not bad. I rate it 6/10

Delgoton has next to no information available for it. Theres actually so little information about it, that when I managed to link-hop my way to its Wikipedia page, I was prompted to write the article for it. This may be the only review of it on the internet. 
Fortunately, there is still some things of interest I could find about Delgoton. It flowers in early May, and is ready to pick in mid-October. When cut, it browns fairly quickly. It was raised at a french nursery called Delbard, who seem to give almost all their new apples names that start with 'Del'. 
Interestingly, Delbard uses irradiation to create new varieties or sports of plants. They call this technique "regenesis", and it works by causing mutations to tissue cells from a seed, and regenerating a bud from the irradiated tissue, which then grows plants which have only a few characteristics that differ from its predecessor.
I'm not sure whether or not the Delgoton variety was a product of regenesis, but it's cool nonetheless.
As for the taste, Delgoton is soft, and not very flavourful. The little flavour it did have was nice though. I didn't enjoy it so much. 3/10

Red dream seems remarkably similar to Honeycrisp. It's just as crisp, and sour with notes of honey. It's close, but I think Honeycrisp is better.
I found almost nothing about this apple online. It has no Wikipedia page, it has no brand page, even the store I bought it from, and the orchard that grew it don't have Red Dream on their websites. Maybe this apple was just a dreamâ¦..
7/10
Chantecler is a fairly average tasting apple with a very refreshing amount of sourness. The flesh is soft, and finely grained. It tastes similar to golden delicious. 6/10

Rubinette is quite a sweet apple, with a sharp honey flavour. It's nice and crisp, but not overly so.
Rubinette is fairly small, and super round. It has some russeting at the stem and base, which probably comes from its parent, Cox. Its other parent is Golden delicious. I'd buy this apple again if I was in the mood for something small and sweet, 7/10

Amber is on the softer side, and fairly sweet. It's a dessert apple, but not too sweet like some can be. It has a nice, soft flavour, though a bit watery. 
The Amber variety is almost 100 years old, being first cultivated sometime before 1936. Its parents are unknown. While looking up this apple, I found an Irish dessert called "Apple Amber." It's like an apple custard pie with meringue, I'd like to make it one day.
I rate this apple 5/10

Kissabel is super flavourful, it's sweet, tangy, and has hints of vanilla and sweet berries. The sweet berry flavour is especially prominent in the dark red flesh area between the stem and the core. The texture is right in between crisp and soft.

Kissabel is a trademark name that covers 6 different varieties. The one I had was most likely Kissabel Y101 from IFO fruit. This varieties parents are Golden Delicious and SJ109, an unpatented apple responsible for Kissabels red flesh. Thanks to Lucy for getting these for me.

The skin is meant to be yellow, but the pink from the inside bleeds out, making it look orange. It has a conical shape, with pronounced lobes near the base like red delicious. The skin is pretty waxy, almost greasy like Aurora Golden Galas.

Red flesh apples like this one are amazing, if you ever have the chance to try any, I highly recommend. I rate Kissabel 10/10!

Crimson crisp has a lot of everything. It's super crisp like the name suggests, but it's also very sweet. Its flavour is quite tart, much more so than I was expecting considering it's a red apple. It seems fairly similar to Kanzi.

Crimson Crisps parents are 2 lab apples you won't find in stores, but it has popular apples like Golden Delicious, Johnathon, and Melba apples in its lineage. It was bred to be resistant to apple scab, and have a long storage life. It can stay ripe on the tree for up to a month before being picked! This apple is available in the US, Italy, and the UK. Thanks again to Lucy for finding this apple.

I rate Crimson Crisp 8/10

Magic star apples are very crisp, and much sweeter than they are sour. The ones I tried were pretty small, like mandarin oranges, though they're normally larger.
Magic star goes by many different names; it's called 'Sprank' in the Netherlands, 'Kentish Kiss' in tesco supermarkets, and 'Natrya' when grown organically. The official name for this apple is SQ159. It was developed in the Netherlands as an apple scab resistant variety.
I rate them 6/10

Robijn is fairly soft and mild, the skin is a bit thick. It tastes a lot like Gala or Jonagold.
The Robijn variety comes from a mutation of a mutation of Jonagold. It has a very long shelf life and is harvested earlier than Jonagold.
I rate Robijn 4/10

Cheerfull gold is a pretty big, tasty dessert apple. It's crisp, and has a strong sour taste evenly balanced with sweetness. It tastes very full, not bland at all. 

Cheerfull Gold is a cross between Cox's Orange Pippen, and Golden delicious. The trees grow many apples, which stay on the branches into winter.

I rate this apple 8/10

Cameo is such a silly shaped apple. The skin is quite pretty, and its colour varies wildly from apple to apple. 
The flavour is fairly mild, and the skin is thick. It tastes okay. 
Cameos parents are unknown, but thought to be Golden Delicious and Red Delicious.
I rate this apple 4/10

Lolipop is sweet! It's very crisp, and one of the sweetest apples I've tried. The branding for this apple calls it the candy fruit, and they're not wrong. It does taste like candy. It's not tart, and has a very mild flavour. It has a bit of a dry, Lady Alice-like taste. 
Lolipop is has a very long storage life, up to 8 months! You can also find this apple under the name "Inored". I would recommend this apple only if you want something quite sweet. I rate it 7/10

Also known as Red Jonaprince, this is a very big and soft apple. The flavour is pretty mild, and similar to red delicious. Red Prince's parents are thought to be Jonathon and Golden Delicious, making it a sibling to Jonagold. Many people believe that Red prince is a sport of Jonagold, but since this apple variety was discovered as a chance seedling, it is unlikely. 
I rate this apple 3/10

Golden Rose is quite juicy and crisp, and just a little more sour than sweet. It has notes of honey. It's grown in france, and there's not much information about it online. 
6/10

Rave is a ridiculously juicy apple, Rave is also quite crisp, flavourful, tart, and pretty. This variety is a cross between Honeycrisp and MonArk, the latter of which is a very early growing apple. Rave ripens in early August, earlier than most other apples. I'm surprised it still tastes good after being in the fridge for so long, its shelf life is very long. I would try this apple again, it was one of the juiciest apples I've eaten so far. I rate it 9/10

The Gravenstein variety is over 350 years old, and is the national apple of Denmark. It's has a very lovely flavour, tart and sweet with hints of toffee. I found the texture to be pretty soft and mealy, though it's probably because the one I tried had been in storage so long.

Gravenstein is a great tasting apple that suffers from a few problems that make it hard to find. The tree is prone to many diseases, and the fruits don't last very long in storage. It has a reputation in North America for being difficult to grow, and is better suited to the milder weather conditions of Europe. Despite this, it tastes good enough for people to keep growing them instead of other, easier to grow varieties. They seem to be a very popular variety for applesauce, because of their complex flavour.

I would like to try another, fresher Gravenstein. The apple I had was good but spent a lot of time in the fridge, so I think my review and rating don't give Gravenstein the credit it deserves. If I end up trying a fresher one, I may come back to this post and adjust the rating. Even though this one had been in the fridge for a while, it had a very unique flavour I'd like to try again. For now, I rate Gravenstein 6/10.

Paula Red was discovered as a chance seedling near a McIntosh orchard, the man who discovered this variety named them after his wife, Pauline. This apple is interesting because its texture changes depending on when you harvest it. Early in the season, Paula red has a crisp, firm bite. When harvested later, the texture becomes soft, like a McIntosh. The taste is sweet and equally sour, with faint floral and strawberry notes. The skin is unfortunately very overpowering. 
This variety has a short shelf life, so my review is probably not as kind as it would be if I had tried a fresher one. It was still nice, but the thick flesh and mealy texture keep it from being an apple that I would be excited to see on the shelf. I rate Paula Red 4/10

Empire is a cross between Red Delicious and McIntosh. Its parentage is pretty obvious, it has thicker skin, like a red delicious, and a similar flavour to both apples. Its flesh is soft. 
Empire is one of the parents of Cosmic Crisp (the other parent being Honeycrisp). Cosmic Crisp apples are a variety developed to taste like a honeycrisp, but more resistant to damage. Empire was chosen as one of the parents because it is more resistant to bruising than other apples, and it still tastes good, unlike other thick skinned apples like Red Delicious.
I rate Empire 6/10

Developed in Minnesota, SweeTango is a cross between Honeycrisp and Zelstar. It's very crisp and juicy, with a sweet tangy taste. It has a long shelf life, not very common among other early season varieties. SweeTango has large juicy cells, making each bite super crunchy, almost like an asian pear. Despite all this, it doesn't really have much flavour besides sweet and sour. I rate it 7/10

Bliss is soft, sweet, and a bit tart. Nothing exceptional about the taste. This apple was a bit strange because the sticker says its from a company called Blue Mountain, but their website doesn't list Bliss as an apple variety that they grow. I give it 4/10

Marketed as "the flavours of autumn", Autumn Glory tastes mildly of caramel and cinnamon. The flavours aren't very subtle, like in other apples. You can easily pick up the notes of caramel and cinnamon, it's incredible.

Autumn Glory is a cross between Fuji and Golden Delicious. Its main flavour is mostly reminiscent of fuji, and it has no sourness to it. I think it would make a good apple sauce, or go well with something savoury like rosemary or thyme on pork. 

The caramel and cinnamon flavours are fairly strong, but they can get lost if you aren't paying attention. If they were a bit stronger, this apple could get a full ten. Overall, the flavour and crispness is awesome, and I rate Autumn Glory 9/10

Mutsu looks like a huge Granny Smith, and tastes pretty similar too. It's very sour and crisp, though it differs from Granny Smith in that the skin is thinner, and it has a faintly sweet aftertaste. The flesh is coarse, and strangely feels almost slightly powdery. Mutsu apples can be green, yellow, or red, depending on how much sunlight they're exposed to after being picked. Like Orin apples, Mutsu is a cross between Indo and Golden Delicious. It seems like a popular apple online, but to me, this apple doesn't live up to its reputation. I rate Mutsu 3/10.

Snow Cloud is the smallest apple variety I've tried yet, each apple is about the size of a nickel. Snow cloud is a type of ornamental crabapple, bred specifically to look nice on the tree. As such, I had very low expectations, but was pleasantly surprised to find it wasn't bad.
These crabapples are very hard. They have an average amount of sweetness, with a really nice bright sourness to them, but are unfortunately accompanied by a mildly bitter skin. Eating these is not convenient, the core is huge relative to the size of the apple, so the slices are even smaller than you would expect, and you get a lot more skin in each bite than you would with a regular sized apple. 
Snow Cloud gets its name from the large amount of white flowers the tree grows in May. The fruits start out yellow, and gradually grow redder as winter sets in. 
Aside from the inconvenience of eating them, and the ridiculousness of rating ornamental crabapples on their taste, I give them a 4/10.

The Elstar variety tastes sweet and honeyed, with a nice spritely sourness to it. The texture is on the softer side of crisp.
A cross between Golden Delicious and Ingrid Marie.
7/10

Winter Banana is a variety I've been searching for ever since I learned of them about 3 years ago. I finally got my hands on a bag at UBC Botanical Gardens Apple Festival, and was not disappointed. 
Though they are rare in markets, the trees are actually common in orchards. The trees are quite hardy, and produce tons of flowers, helping to pollinate other trees on the orchard. The apples don't often make it to customers, because they bruise very easily, making it difficult to transport them. 
Their texture starts out fairly crisp, and softens as they age. The ones I had were between soft and crisp, and shyly sweet. Sourness is almost completely absent from the taste. What sets this apple apart from others are the faint tropical notes of pineapple and banana, which is especially prominent when eating the apple in small slices. It was a kind of strange flavour, but it was tasty. 
Winter Banana browns really fast, noticeable within a couple minutes. They are a chance seedling with unknown parents. From what I've read, they keep well, but quickly lose their distinctive flavour when in storage. In addition to a banana-like flavour, this variety is banana-yellow, with a lovely pink blush and the flesh is a creamy white. You can tell they are ripe when they give off a faint banana-like aroma, which I noticed when opening my bag of them. The fruits occasionally have small ridges running from top to bottom. All of these things tie in to give the apple the name 'Winter Banana'.
I rate winter banana a 7/10. You probably won't notice the distinctive flavour unless you eat one thats very fresh, but even without that, the apple is quite good.

Easter Orange is sweet, very dry, intense, similar to a bosc pear without the grainy texture. Intense flavour,  pretty dense and hard. Not juicy. A very interesting looking apple, I don't think I've ever seen such a prominent orange colouring on an apple before.
The apples are very long lasting, can stay in storage through the winter until march, giving it the name easter orange. I rate this apple 6/10.

Golden Russet is the second russet apple I've had the chance to try, and it certainly lived up to my expectations. The flavour is incredible, it's tart and subtly sweet, with strong overtones of caramel and molasses, and hints of nuttiness and apple pie spice. It's similar to the Autumn Glory variety, but with more pronounced flavour. The only downside of this apple is the flesh is pretty dense and tough, like biting into an unripe pear. The flavour is excellent though, which is why this apple is primarily used for cider. I rate it 7/10

Lady (Api) is nearly a 400 year old variety, and quite famous. I was really excited to have the chance to try this apple, and a bit shocked at how small it was. 
Historically, they've been used both for eating, and as decoration, particularity in Christmas wreaths and garlands. Lady used to be an umbrella term that referred to many types of apples, but has since become the name for this variety specifically.
The skin has a fairly strong granny smith like taste to it, but otherwise the apple is quite nice. It's sweet and bright, but not overwhelmingly so. I was pleasantly surprised by its notes of citrus and floral.
7/10

Winesap has crisp flesh that falls apart as if melting in your mouth, paired with a really nice flavour, vinous as the name implies, equally tangy and sweet. It's fairly juicy, and quite large, but it suffers from tough and thick skin. Winesap is often used in ciders. Great flavour and nice texture, but it's held back by its thick skin. 6/10.

Sekai Ichi, aka World #1, is absolutely huge! It almost weighs a full pound.
Sekai Ichi means "Worlds number one" in Japanese, and if you like sweet, delicately flavoured apples, this might be the one for you.  This variety is very crisp and sweet, with not even a hint of sourness to it. It has a similar mellow honeyed flavour to fuji, with floral notes. However, without any acidity to balance it out, the taste becomes almost sickly sweet. 
Flavour aside, it is a very beautiful and impressive apple, one of the largest I've ever tried. If you love sweet apples, I would give this a try, but the lack of acidity and light flavour leads me to rate Sekai Ichi 6/10.

Discovery is a soft apple, but not mushy in the way some soft apples are. The texture is very smooth, almost buttery. mild sweet flavour. Not super juicy, or tart. Tastes like it would pair excellently with a hard cheese. Some people say this apple has notes of strawberry, but I didn't taste it. 
Discovery apples are thought to be a cross between Worcester Pearmain and Beauty of Bath. This variety is very beautiful, and used primarily for apple sauce. Maybe I will make apple sauce with it, because the flavour and texture seem to be perfect for it.
7/10

Crawley Beauty is between soft and crisp. Nice light, tart flavour, but nothing special. The skin is a bit thick, best if peeled. 
Taste-wise, this apple is pretty average. It is quite nice looking though, like the name suggests. The flesh is remarkably white, with a bit of pink/red bleeding in from the skin.
I rate this variety 5/10

Chinook is one of the many varieties that is a result of Gala and Splendour. The apple breeding program in Summerland B.C. released this Chinook to the public in 1997, alongside the Silken and Creston varieties.
Chinnok is firm, refreshingly tart, with a balanced amount of sugar, though not notably juicy. Tastes pretty average, I rate it 5/10

Johnathan is soft, and with thick skin. It is sweet, but not overly so, and is complimented by a good amount of tartness. The flavour is very light. 
Johnathan used to be a very popular apple variety, and is a parent of the once famed Jonagold apple. Both varieties have largely faded from commercial production, having been overshadowed by modern varieties like Gala and Honeycrisp. 
This apple was alright, the thick skin and texture made it a bit unappealing though. I rate Johnathan 4/10

Not to be confused with 'Royal Court', Court Royal is a sport of the Cortland apple. Court Royal is a big burly apple. Its flesh is soft but not mealy. The flavour is nice and complex.
Originally grown as a cider apple, it is also good for fresh eating. 
5/10

Snow apple is very soft, and ever so slightly tart with a delicate sweet vinous flavour. Skin is on the thicker side. Like Discovery apples, some people say this variety has a hint of strawberry flavour, but I haven't noticed it. This variety was given the name Snow Apple, because of its bright white flesh. It's also known as Fameuse, as it originated in Quebec, nearly 300 years ago. This variety is a parent of MacIntosh.
Like MacIntosh, the Snow Apple is likely better when picked fresh off the tree. However, this one surely hasn't been in storage for that long, and so I rate it 3/10, for its thick skin and exceedingly soft flesh.

Dazzle is very crisp and juicy, with a very sweet candy like flavour, though it's a bit watery. It reminds me of a watermelon. Seems like it would go really well in a salad. 
Dazzle is a cross between Sweetie and Scired, and like the Jazz and Envy varieties, it comes from New Zealand. 
7/10

Gloster 69 is a small, crisp and sweet apple, with a little underlying tartness. It seems like a better Red Delicious, but is still not that great. It has thick skin, and slightly mealy flesh. 
Released in 1969 (which is why it has '69' in it's name), this variety is very hardy. The trees can survive low temperatures, and the fruits can stay in cold storage for longer than many varieties. 
4/10

They are not kidding, Evercrisp is crisp!! Cutting this apple into slices sounds like splitting wood, and chewing it overpowers every other sound around you. It also has quite the bold candied flavour, refreshingly sour and extremely sweet. On top of that, it's also very juicy, and not watery in the slightest. It's a very overpowering apple, every aspect is pushed to 200%. 
Evercrisp is a cross between Honeycrisp and Fuji, and tastes as if you took every bit of each apple, and compressed it into one. 
I really like the extreme crispness of this apple, as well as it's prominent flavour, and juiciness. I'm not really a fan of how sweet it is though, it reminds me of Inored. I rate Evercrisp an 7/10

Red Rome is a sport of the 'Rome' variety, and it has a very deep red skin that the original doesn't. It seems to have slightly more russeting than most varieties. Very interestingly, the red colouration seems to continue on the inside of the apple, drawing a vibrant border between the core and the flesh. I've never seen this so pronounced in an apple before. 

This variety is supposed to be one of the best for baking. It holds its shape well, and develops its flavour as it cooks. 

When eaten raw, it has a sweet and subtle candy-like flavour, and no notable sourness. It's pretty dry, which is to be expected given the apples eagerness to russet. Its texture is soft and slightly mealy. 
Raw taste rating: 3/10

Arkansas Black is similar to McIntosh or Winesap, with a tart vinous flavour. Slightly dry, and quite crisp. Dense flesh. The skin is really dark, like black or purple in some places. This apple is keeps very well, and mellows out in storage, becoming sweeter and less tart. I rate it 6/10

Scarlet Spur is crisp yet soft to cut into. Flavourful, more sweet than sour, but not lacking in sourness. It's related to Red Delicious, and tastes similar, with a more pronounced floral flavour, and without the wretched mealy texture. It seems like a much better Red Delicious, if you enjoy that apple I suggest you try this one. 

In the same way that Scarlet Spur improves upon Red Delicious, there is an apple variety called Scarlet Spur II, which supposedly takes these improvements even further. I'd like to try it some day. 

I rate Scarlet Spur a 7/10.

Melrose is a sweet apple with a refreshing amount of acidity, and not shy on flavour. Notes of citrus. The skin is a bit thick, but when peeled this apple is said to be excellent for pie. It lasts impressively long in storage, and grows sweeter as it ages. 

Melrose was very popular as a home-grown apple in the USA, and is touted online as a very American apple. It is the offical state apple of Ohio. 
I rate Melrose a 7/10
Sinta is a soft apple with an almost buttery texture. Has a nice sweetness to it and no notable acidity. Quite flavourful, a bit like honey. It tastes like a better version of Golden Delicious. 7/10

Newtown Pippin is crisp and tart. Not quite as sour as Granny Smith, and with thinner skin. The flavour is refreshing and spritely. It is a good apple.

It's a nearly 300 year old American variety, and Benjamin Franklins favourite kind of apple.  It peaked in popularity in victorian England, even though the variety doesn't grow well in the UKs cool climate. Newtown pippin needs a hot summer and autumn, after which the variety ripens in late October, and tastes best after at least 1-2 months of storage

I rate Newtown Pippin 6/10

Snapdragon is very crisp, similar flavour and texture to Kanzi and honeycrisp, though it seems sweeter than either. Fairly juicy, it's quite a good apple.

Snapdragon is a smaller apple, about the size of a fist. It was developed recently by Cornell University, and it is the result of a cross between honeycrisp and an unnamed cultivar that was part of the universities breeding program. Supposedly, the apple has subtle notes of vanilla and melon, but I didn't pick up on them. 

Despite this, the apple is very flavourful with a satisfying crunch. I rate Snapdragon 8/10

Originating in New Zealand, Posy apples are a cross between the Royal Gala and New Zealand Rose varieties. Posy apples have existed for ~20 years, but only just became available globally in 2023. 
They are pretty apples, and taste remarkably similar to an asian pear. The flavour is light though a bit watery, decently sweet with no trace of sourness. Texture-wise, the apple is quite crisp with thin skin. Overall a decent pick if you like sweet apples. 
I rate Posy 6/10

Another new variety from New Zealand. Roxy is the first registered apple variety developed by the Fashion Foods company. The apple is related to Gala, though it resembles Smitten, with a wide lobed base and light russeting at the top. Its exact parents are unknown to the general public; I've reached out to one of the people who developed the apple but have not yet received a response.

Roxy was developed to look pretty for consumers, and it does that well. The taste however, is nothing special. The flavour is mild, and similar to Gala or Golden Delicious. It's a bit sweet, with some trace amounts of tart. The flesh is on the softer side, though not mealy.

This variety ripens early in the season, about a week before Gala ripens. It is likely better when fresh off the tree, but so are most apples. I rate Roxy 4/10.

Tarzi is a sport of the Galaxy Gala apple, making it 4 sports removed from the original Gala variety. It's another nice variety from New Zealand

It tastes like a mix between Gala and Honeycrisp, with a sweet flavour and a pronounced tartness, accompanied by a mild floral taste. It's fairly average in terms of juiciness and crunch, but the flavour is pleasant. I rate Tarzi 6/10

Galamac is a cross between Gala, and Jersey Mac. The latter of which is related to the famous MacIntosh. It's a fairly new apple, patent still pending, and not a lot of information is available online for it.

Galamac is a great apple. It's sweet, juicy, tart, and has a hint of pear or Fuji. The flesh is crisp yet a bit soft; it's not crunchy, but has a satisfying bite. Its thin skin goes almost unnoticeable, and in my opinion, Galamac is just the right size for an apple.

If you find Galamac at a local farmers market, I suggest you try one for yourself! I rate this variety 8/10

Wolf River is absolutely huge. You could probably make a pie with just two of them. It's fairly dense, and eye-wateringly sour. Not sweet, and slightly dry, though it has a unique aftertaste. Perfect for baking. 

Wolf river is a chance seedling, which was discovered on the shores of the Wolf River in Wisconsin. It is known as one of the best varieties for making apple butter, with the result being rich and fluffy.

By raw taste rating, this is a 2/10. It's not meant for eating raw, it's meant for baking. Such a big and tart apple, it's hard to get through.

Zestar! is another great apple developed in Minnesota. Yes, the exclamation point is part of its name. This apple comes with a pronounced tart taste, accompanied by more sweetness than usual for a sour apple. Tastes like a watered down SweetTart candy. Skin is unfortunately on the thicker side. 
Not super crisp, but not soft. Nice light texture. If you prefer sour apples, this is definitely something you should try.
I rate it a high 7/10, could've been 8 of not for the thick skin

Also known as Swiss Gourmet, Arlet is a fairly nice though unimpressive apple. It's sweet and tart, though the flavour is quite mild. Very dense, like Envy apples. The skin is just barely noticeably thick. 
I rate Arlet 5/10
